chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whom the enemy met, and they took from him wealth or belongings. Then the Muslims captured that. How should the man's belongings be treated? He said: 'If they took it before they secured the man's belongings, it is returned to him. And if they took it after they had secured it, it is Fay' (booty) for the Muslims, and they have more right to pre-emption.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةِ: pre-emption or right of first refusal
key_terms.فَيْءٌ: booty or spoils of war acquired without fighting
key_terms.يَحُوزُوا: to secure or take possession of

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on property taken by enemies from Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the critical legal distinction between *Ghanimah* (spoils of war) and *Fay'* (booty) based on the enemy's possession status (*ihraz*) of the captured property. It highlights the Shia juristic view that once the enemy secures the goods, they transition to communal Muslim ownership, granting them the right of pre-emption (*shuf'ah*), a nuance often discussed in contrast to Sunni schools regarding the timing of possession.
